title: Speed Webb's arrangers and the car that went into the canal
summary: Speed Webb's band had seven arrangers, one of whom, Chuck Ross, died when his car went off the road into a canal in Canada.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: It was a good band. All the bands I played with they were -- they were very good bands. Especially Steve Webb. I tell you Steve Webb had one of the greatest bands -- it's just too bad it never did get recorded. And it's too bad Thamon Hayes never did get recorded at the time, you know. But --
Both -- both those bands had good arrangers and that was very important I guess.
Yeah, Steve Webb had seven guys arranging in Steve Webb's band. You know -- they had Teddy arrange, Gus arrange. Joe arranged. You know -- Joe Ellis.

Leonard Gay (PHONETIC) arranged and a guy -- a boy by the name of Chuck Ross (PHONETIC). He arranged. He got killed in the canal up there in Canada. He was there -- he went off on the ice or something one night after they was finished work they was going from Montreal back to Detroit. And they went off the road into the canal -- river -- you know -- when they was fixing the St. Lawrence --

They went off in there and they didn't find them until four or five months after the snow had thawed -- they found them. They had went off the road. When they disappeared no one knew what had happened to them. This happened about -- well I guess maybe ten years ago or maybe a little more -- 15 probably. But that's -- that's right. And I thought that was the worst thing -- I got sick thinking about that. You know, it was his wife -- he and his wife and I guess somebody else were in the car. They went off the road into that thing. Boy, that's a drag, you know. I think we ought to have a little breakfast don't you think and then we can have --
